paragraphs: Ireland has joined a new world plan to protect peatlands. Peatlands are wet lands with a lot of old plant material.
The plan is called the Peatland Breakthrough. It started at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey. Germany, Peru and Uganda have also joined.
The plan wants to raise 100 billion dollars. By 2030, it wants to repair at least 30 million hectares of damaged peatland.
Peatlands are small, but they hold a lot of carbon. When people dry them out, the carbon goes into the air. This makes climate change worse.
About 21% of Ireland is peatland. Ireland recently repaired 24,500 hectares of bog. Now it will share what it learned with other countries.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭加入了一項保護泥炭地的全球新計畫。
泥炭地是含有大量古老植物物質的濕地。
這項計畫叫做「泥炭地突破」。
它在土耳其的 COP31 氣候會談上啟動。
德國、秘魯和烏干達也已加入。
這項計畫希望籌集 1000 億美元。
到 2030 年，它希望修復至少 3000 萬公頃受損的泥炭地。
泥炭地面積不大，但儲存了大量的碳。
當人們把泥炭地弄乾，碳就會進入空氣。
這會讓氣候變遷更嚴重。
愛爾蘭約有 21% 的土地是泥炭地。
愛爾蘭最近修復了 24,500 公頃的泥炭沼澤。
現在它將與其他國家分享學到的經驗。

paragraphs: Ireland is one of the first countries to join a new international plan to save the world's peatlands. The plan, called the Peatland Breakthrough, was launched at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey.
Germany, Peru and Uganda have also signed up, and Canada supports the plan. It aims to raise 100 billion dollars for peatland projects around the world.
By 2030, the plan wants to stop the loss of healthy peatlands and to start repairing at least 30 million hectares of damaged ones.

Peatlands cover only 3–4% of the Earth's land, but they store up to one third of all the carbon in the world's soil. When they are drained or damaged, they release this carbon and add to global warming.

About 21% of Ireland is peatland, but very little of it is still healthy. Climate Minister Darragh O'Brien said Ireland will share its experience, including one of the world's biggest bog repair projects, which covered 24,500 hectares.
sentZh: 愛爾蘭是首批加入一項拯救全球泥炭地新國際計畫的國家之一。
這項名為「泥炭地突破」的計畫，在土耳其安塔利亞舉行的 COP31 氣候會談上啟動。
德國、秘魯和烏干達也已加入，加拿大則表態支持。

泥炭地只佔地球陸地的 3% 到 4%，卻儲存了全球土壤中多達三分之一的碳。
當泥炭地被排乾或受損時，就會釋放這些碳，加劇全球暖化。

By 2030, it seeks to halt the loss of healthy peatlands and place at least 30 million hectares of degraded land under restoration.

Although peatlands cover just 3–4% of the planet's land surface, they store up to a third of all soil carbon. When drained or damaged, they release that carbon and become a major source of greenhouse gases.
